title: The Personification of Charity
clues: 14th-century Middle English allegorical narrative poem by William Langland.
Composed in unrhymed alliterative verse.
The protagonist appears finally in the likeness of a biblical figure.
forensics: In Langland's Piers Plowman (1370–90), Piers appears finally as The Good Samaritan (or Jesus).

title: The Tabard Inn Agreement
clues: Middle English collection of 24 stories spanning over 17,000 lines.
The Host Harry Bailly proposes a storytelling competition on the pilgrimage to Canterbury.
The total number of tales agreed per pilgrim.
forensics: The host suggested each pilgrim tell four stories in all (two on the way to Canterbury and two on the return journey).

title: The Ovidian Narrative
clues: A long narrative poem published in 1592–1593.
Plot is based on passages from Ovid's Metamorphoses.
Focuses on unrequited love, desire, and mortality.
forensics: Venus and Adonis is a narrative poem by William Shakespeare written in 1592-1593.

title: The Quarto Collection of 1609
clues: Written primarily in iambic pentameter with rhyme scheme ABAB CDCD EFEF GG.
126 are addressed to a Fair Youth, and 28 to a Dark Lady.
Identify the total number of sonnets published in this sequence.
forensics: Shakespeare published a sequence of 154 sonnets covering themes of time, love, and beauty.

title: The Maltese Machiavel
clues: Written by Christopher Marlowe in 1589 or 1590.
Set against a conflict between Spain and the Ottoman Empire.
The prologue is spoken by the ghost of Machiavelli himself.
forensics: Barabas in Marlowe's 'The Jew of Malta' is explicitly identified as 'a sound Machiavil'.

title: The Mock-Heroic Royalist
clues: A 17th-century English mock-heroic narrative poem.
Written in iambic tetrameter couplets with feminine rhymes.
Satirizes religious factions and Puritan hypocrisy after Don Quixote.
forensics: Hudibras is an English mock-heroic narrative poem written by Samuel Butler.

title: The Melancholy Octosyllables
clues: Published in the 1645 Poems collection by Humphrey Moseley.
Companion piece to 'L'Allegro'.
Celebrates the contemplative life in octosyllabic couplets.
options: On the Late Massacre in Piedmont
forensics: John Milton wrote 'Il Penseroso' in octosyllabic couplets as a reflection on poetic melancholy.

title: The Restoration Sequel Scandal
clues: A 1696 Restoration comedy subtitled 'Virtue in Danger'.
Written as a direct sequel to Colley Cibber's 'Love's Last Shift'.
Authored by an architect-playwright, not William Congreve.
forensics: 'The Relapse' was written by Sir John Vanbrugh, while the other three plays are by William Congreve.

title: The Roman World Well Lost
clues: Heroic drama in blank verse written in 1677.
Strictly observes the classical unities of time, place, and action.
John Dryden's acknowledged adaptation of Shakespeare's Roman play.
forensics: Dryden's 'All for Love' (1677) is an adaptation of Shakespeare's 'Antony and Cleopatra'.

title: The Sovereign Sea Monster
clues: Published in 1651 during the English Civil War.
Advocates for a strong sovereign authority to avoid a state of nature that is 'solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short'.
Written by Thomas Hobbes.
forensics: Thomas Hobbes published 'Leviathan' in 1651 propounding social contract theory.
